## Findings
- claim-1: The 2011 paper conjectures minimality of both Theorem 5.4 generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\). [source-6@L14-L16|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: The stronger, distinct statement is \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}/\Lambda_+J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\). [source-6@L56-L72|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-3: The escalated DOI candidate is St. Dizier–Yong (2024), *Presenting the cohomology of a Schubert variety: Proof of the minimality conjecture*; its abstract says “We prove the minimality conjecture.” [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832]
## Strategy
Automatic DOI escalation for `10.1112/jlms.12832` was inspected. It retrieved metadata and the abstract-level statement “We prove the minimality conjecture,” but no bounded primary full-text theorem passage. The requested theorem-text certificate therefore could not be completed or independently reviewed.

**Requested target established: no.** The 2024 result is not theorem-level established from supplied evidence.

## Gaps
Missing exact 2024 primary-source text with stable locators for: hypotheses, coefficient ring, definitions of \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), the two generating families, and the numbered minimality conclusion.

The stronger claim
\[
J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}/\Lambda_+J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}
\cong \mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}
\]
remains separately unestablished; abstract-level minimality does not imply torsion-freeness or this integral isomorphism.

## Next
Ingest bounded numbered full-text passages from the DOI source (or exact matching arXiv full text), with artifact digest and page/line mappings, then compare its theorem line-by-line with the 2011 conjecture and separately check for any indecomposables statement.
